clue.text: Over-sensitive to crappy garlic — the French included

indicators.note: something crappy is in a bad state, so these letters are knocked out of order
included means placed inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone who reacts badly to cheap garlic, the French being blamed as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergic person's immune system overreacts to a substance, so they are abnormally sensitive to it.

clue.text: To capture Blair's heart, Gordon playing the old soldier

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
playing suggests the letters are being played about with and moved around
to capture something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the central letter of Blair
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown wins Tony Blair over by pretending to be a battle-scarred veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: Playing the old soldier is an idiom for feigning hardship, which hides that playing is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, a type of soldier from past centuries.

clue.text: Place for fairies? Got out, but without balls

indicators.note: out means put out of place, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
without is used in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged word wraps around another

blocks.note: taken as written
balls is slang for nonsense, which is rot

explanation.surface: A camp fairy-tale setting, then someone who has escaped, castrated.
explanation.walkthrough: Without is the old word for outside, not lacking. Balls here means nonsense rather than anatomy, a common British use.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairies are traditionally pictured living in a grotto, a small cave, and Santa's grotto is a Christmas tradition; the question mark flags the playful fit.

clue.text: Leg over, writhing, I get in jelly

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read from the other end
writhing means twisting about, so these letters are wriggled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sex (a leg-over) with much writhing, ending up covered in jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg-over is British slang for sex, which hides that over is a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is a jelly-like high explosive, and jelly is its common slang name among safe-crackers.

clue.text: Fruity luvvie caught with Grant …

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
to grant permission is to allow

explanation.surface: A plummy-voiced theatrical type is caught in the act with Hugh Grant, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 8 Across for the surface only; each answer has its own wordplay. Simon Callow co-starred with Hugh Grant in Four Weddings and a Funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Callow is a flamboyant English stage actor, the kind of theatrical figure the British press calls a fruity luvvie.

clue.text: Ex-con Brenda abandoned — shrewd!

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: Jeffrey Archer, the novelist jailed for perjury in 2001
Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda, and ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A former prisoner dumped by the Queen proves himself clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means knowing and cunning, a sly shrewdness, as in an arch look.

clue.text: Flog musical composition collection

blocks.note: to flog is to whip
a round is a song in which voices enter in turn, like Frere Jacques

explanation.surface: Selling off a set of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Flog looks like British slang for sell, but here it means to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal collection of money among a group, for a gift or a good cause.

clue.text: … bum to bum, dead tight

blocks.note: a bum is a worthless person, and so is a rat
the buttocks, in British slang
D is the standard abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: Carrying on from 5 Across: two men pressed buttock to buttock, very close indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dead tight reads as one phrase, but dead is wordplay and tight alone is the definition, British slang for drunk. The word bum is used twice with two meanings, a scoundrel then a backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, and rat-arsed is a cruder British word for very drunk.

clue.text: Times includes a load of crap

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time, here doubled for the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dig at The Times newspaper for printing rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Times looks like the newspaper, but it is two lots of the time abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is cheap worthless rubbish, so a load of it is crap in the junk sense.

clue.text: Son, being a sailor means shagging

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
serving as one of a ship's crew

explanation.surface: A parent hears that their boy joining the navy will lead to sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Shagging is British slang for having sex, and screwing is a synonym in the same vulgar register.

clue.text: Bristol chip snack

blocks.note: Bristols means breasts, from rhyming slang Bristol City for titty
a chip is a small piece

explanation.surface: A packet of crisps or a bag of chips bought in the city of Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristol looks like the English city, but it is rhyming slang: Bristol City rhymes with titty, so Bristols are breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small tasty morsel of food, a light snack.

clue.text: Flash character gets to give a roasting to champing-at-the-bit politician

blocks.note: Flash Gordon is the comic-strip space hero
to brown meat is to roast or sear it

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero gets to lay into an impatient politician.
explanation.walkthrough: To give a roasting usually means to tell someone off, but here it is the cook's sense, browning meat.
explanation.definitionFit: In 2006 Chancellor Gordon Brown was famously impatient for Tony Blair to stand down so he could become Prime Minister.

clue.text: Den collared by champs (no lovers of 12)

indicators.note: something collared is grabbed and held, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: to champ is to bite
an animal's den is its lair

explanation.surface: A cosy hideout seized by winners who dislike the politician in 12.
explanation.walkthrough: Champs looks like champions, but it is the verb to champ, to chew noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of Tony Blair were known for their rivalry and hostility towards Gordon Brown's camp.

clue.text: Kill Tony off about mid-Dec and go stuff yourself

indicators.note: mid takes just the middle letter of the abbreviation it is attached to
off and about both suggest letters knocked out of place and moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
the central letter of Dec, the abbreviation of December

explanation.surface: A plot to bump off Tony Blair before Christmas, met with a rude brush-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Kill Tony off reads like a murder plot; off is the anagram signal, and only the middle letter of Dec is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Not likely is an emphatic refusal, the polite equivalent of telling someone to go stuff themselves.

clue.text: Grope and come together in an excited state

blocks.note: two things that come together make contact
to be up is to be stirred up or aroused

explanation.surface: A sequence of fumbling, meeting and arousal.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch someone up is British slang for fondling them sexually without consent, which is groping.

clue.text: Lavatory crap — needs a musical setting

blocks.note: the can is American slang for the toilet
tat is cheap worthless rubbish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that toilet humour would be better set to music.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a choral composition, often a sacred text set to music for voices and orchestra.

clue.text: They might well reveal Blair's behind in unusual hot spell

definitions.text: They might well reveal Blair's behind

indicators.note: unusual means not in the ordinary form, so these letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Skimpy summer clothes in a heatwave showing off the Prime Minister's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind looks like a bottom; it means trailing, as Blair's Labour Party was behind in opinion surveys.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinion surveys measure party support, so they would show Tony Blair trailing his rivals.

clue.text: Out of Ben and Lisa, the one who's not straight?

indicators.note: out of here means made from, the letters being rebuilt into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Of a man and a woman in a couple, which is the gay one?
explanation.definitionFit: Straight is slang for heterosexual, so someone not straight is gay; the question mark admits the definition is broad.

clue.text: PM Harold (star comedian) linked with Brown, the never-to-be Labour leader

blocks.note: Harold Lloyd was a star comedian of silent films
George Brown was Labour deputy leader who lost the 1963 leadership contest to Harold Wilson

explanation.surface: A trivia question pairing Prime Minister Harold Wilson with the Labour man who never got the top job.
explanation.walkthrough: PM Harold makes you think of Wilson or Macmillan, but PM is the definition on its own; the Harold wanted is the silent-film comic.
explanation.definitionFit: David Lloyd George was the Liberal Prime Minister of Britain from 1916 to 1922.

clue.text: "Balls to politician!" a hard band member's outburst

blocks.note: balls are round, like two letter Os
a Member of Parliament
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A musician bellows a curse at a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls to is a British exclamation of contempt; here it simply supplies two round letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oompah is the deep repeated sound of a tuba in a brass band, the noise that member makes.

clue.text: Arse has fellow's documents

blocks.note: British slang for the backside
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that a man's papers are only fit for wiping his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from bumfodder, slang for toilet paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is British slang for tedious paperwork, especially official forms and leaflets.

clue.text: One member gobbled by broadcaster is inadequate

indicators.note: something gobbled is swallowed, so it ends up inside the word that eats it

blocks.note: Sky is the British satellite broadcaster
the Roman numeral for one
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A lone MP swallowed up by a TV channel makes a poor showing.
explanation.walkthrough: Member sounds like a limb, but here it is a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy means too small or scanty, which is to say not enough or inadequate.

clue.text: Loafer stuck up male

indicators.note: in a down clue, stuck up means the word is read upward, bottom to top

blocks.note: a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A lazy layabout who is a snobbish man.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuck up looks like snobbish; in a down clue it turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A yob is a loutish idle youth who hangs around, close to a loafer or layabout.

clue.text: Arse operation without normal unblocking initially — keep it firmly shut!

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: butt is slang for the backside
the usual short form of operation
N is the abbreviation for normal
the opening letter of unblocking

explanation.surface: Advice to a patient after bowel surgery: keep that orifice clenched.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like it means lacking, but it means outside: OP goes round the N and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Button up is a command to stop talking, to keep your mouth firmly closed.

clue.text: The Palace: Brenda's last joint supporter left inside

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the name before it
inside means one piece is placed within the others

blocks.note: the final letter of Brenda
L is the abbreviation for left
a ham is a joint of meat
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Gossip about the Queen at Buckingham Palace and her final hip replacement and bra.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II; joint suggests a hip but is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress complex in Granada, Spain.

clue.text: 'Kinky Lips' has two females on grass

indicators.note: kinky means twisted or bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a person nicknamed Kinky Lips in a threesome on a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass looks like a lawn, but it is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for cannabis, and a spliff is a cannabis cigarette, so the answer is defined by its contents.
